task:
Replacing a value with a table gives wrong TOML when dotted keys are involved. Fix all of these.

A duplicated prefix. With doc = parse('fruit.apple = true
'), doc['fruit'] = {'a': 1} must make doc.as_string() exactly '[fruit]
a = 1
', and parse(doc.as_string())['fruit'] must equal {'a': 1}. Today the dotted prefix stays on the new header.

A header that captures a following sibling. The new table must move past every entry that still renders inline, so that the next parse does not nest those entries under it.

With doc = parse('a.b = 1
c.d = 2
'), doc['a'] = {} must render exactly 'c.d = 2

[a]
', and parse(doc.as_string()) must equal {'c': {'d': 2}, 'a': {}}.

With the same start, doc['a'] = {'x': 9} must render exactly 'c.d = 2

[a]
x = 9
', and parse(doc.as_string()) must equal {'c': {'d': 2}, 'a': {'x': 9}}.

The same applies when a plain value becomes a table ahead of a dotted key. With doc = parse('x = 1
c.d = 2
'), doc['x'] = {} must render exactly 'c.d = 2

[x]
', and parse(doc.as_string()) must equal {'c': {'d': 2}, 'x': {}}.

Everything else must keep working.
accept: PYTHONPATH=.bench-deps python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/test_toml_tests.py
